Runic 2.11.2

  • System theme: the orange, purple and cyan accents are darker in light appearance, so they keep 3:1 contrast on the light window (they sat near 2.2:1). Dark appearance is unchanged. Theme JSON can now give a color as "#LIGHT|#DARK".
  • Muse Code: when the CLI's usage card reads "Subscription · Currently unavailable", Runic says so straight away instead of waiting out a 45-second timeout on every refresh.
  • Qwen: DashScope answering 404 for the usage endpoint is no longer logged as an error on each refresh; the card still shows ledger data.

View full changelog

Runic 2.11.1

  • The app icon is the current teal one. Icon.icns had not been rebuilt since January, so the app, the Dock and the website still showed the pre-July blue gradient; it is regenerated from Icon.icon.
  • About: a Docs button opens runic.srinivas.dev; the link row no longer wraps "GitHub" on the terminal-style themes.
  • The screenshot-mode placeholder email is demo@runic.srinivas.dev.

View full changelog

Runic 2.11.0

  • Skins: themes are now built on a skin kit instead of per-theme branches scattered through the views. A skin composes the panel's pages (provider card, overview, resets) and supplies the chrome slots the shared surfaces ask for (panel, tabs, chips, action rows, section headers, notes, footer, the popover frame); any slot a skin leaves alone renders the standard way, and a theme picks its kit with "skin" in its JSON. Gazette moved onto the kit unchanged. Sumi is the first theme built on it end to end: ink on washi — the provider's name in Shippori Mincho under a vermilion hanko cut with the brand mark, each window as a vertical-labelled stanza with a thin Mincho numeral and a brush-stroke gauge over a dry line, the account as a key-value list, the forecast as a note under a small indigo seal; the overview sets the day's average inside an ensō with a one-line read beside it and every provider under its seal; resets are Mincho countdowns with banked resets on a seal; sections open under dry-brush rules, nothing is boxed, the chosen tab is a vermilion stamp, and the page closes with the edition and the author's seal. Shippori Mincho and Zen Kaku Gothic New are bundled as Latin subsets (SIL Open Font License).
  • Blueprint is drawn as an engineering sheet on the kit (Drafting): sheet-index tabs, a title-block masthead with DWG NO and REV, a legend with a CHECKED stamp, each window as a dimensioned bar — extension lines, an arrowed dimension broken by the percent, 45° hatching for the used share, a dashed amber plan line carrying the pace delta, a lettered detail callout — the account as a ruled cell grid, numbered notes beside a revisions table, crop marks, a "General arrangement" front page, a "Schedule of resets" table and a title-block footer. Geist and Geist Mono throughout.
  • Claude: the monthly API credits a Max plan includes (since 7 Oct 2026: $100 on Max 5x, $200 on Max 20x, spent on the API, the Console and the Agent SDK, not on Claude Code) now show under Usage credits — "API credits $200.00 a month · next grant Nov 3". The amount comes from the plan tier Runic already reads; the date from the claude.ai subscription when the claude.ai switch is on. Pro and Free carry no grant and show nothing. The remaining balance is not shown: it lives in the Console, behind a login Runic does not hold.
  • Retro is drawn as a 1970s bench instrument on the kit (Instrument): cream enamel with a bevel and corner screws, keycap tabs that press in, PWR and LINK lamps, an engraved masthead with an olive LCD status strip, each window as a VU meter with a red zone and a needle plus an LCD readout, a pace plate of LED segments, LINK / CAP / BALANCE lamps, engraved label · LCD readout rows, a master meter and segmented channel bars on the front page, a 7-day LED bargraph, reset timers on one LCD, a counter for banked resets, an orange PING keycap and a serial plate footer. Archivo Narrow and Space Mono (OFL).
  • Three new themes, each a skin that changes the metaphor rather than the colours. Departures is a Solari split-flap board: every reset is a departure with a time, a gate (the provider), a remaining-time flap and an OPEN / OUT / HELD / DUE status, under a masthead that flips to the next reset, with gate cards, a board ticker and a yellow REFRESH BOARD key (Barlow Condensed, OFL). Flight deck is an avionics primary flight display in B612, the Airbus cockpit face: vertical tapes with caution bands and a cyan pointer, a green trend vector from the burn rate, an attitude indicator whose horizon pitches with the pace deficit, a MASTER CAUT annunciator, flight-mode cells and resets as waypoints. Receipt prints every ping on thermal paper: line items with dotted leaders, a subtotal, "YOU SAVED n RESETS", a rotated ALL CLEAR / EXHAUSTED stamp, a barcode of the timestamp and torn edges, out of a dark printer slot (Courier Prime, OFL).
  • About: the author link pointed at the wrong X account since the first release. It now opens x.com/_sriinnu_ (About window and Settings → About).
  • Fonts: picking a monospaced family (Berkeley Mono, JetBrains Mono, Commit Mono…) no longer breaks a theme's own display faces. The picker's design override was applied to every font in the panel, and SwiftUI re-resolved the theme's bundled faces through it — Gazette's Fraunces and Manrope silently fell back to the picked mono font at small sizes. The override now applies only to the SF families, and the Gazette page pins its faces.
  • Theme fonts now actually render. In 2.10.0 the per-theme typeface was wired up but never took effect on existing installs — the font picker kept the old literal "Mona Sans" default instead of the new Theme default, so the follow never kicked in and both new themes drew in Mona Sans. The theme-follow default now applies: Terminal renders in JetBrains Mono (mono console), Gazette in its editorial serif, and other themes keep Mona Sans; any family you pick still overrides. Existing installs are nudged onto Theme default once, and an explicit Mona Sans pick afterwards still sticks.
  • Gazette is now a proper editorial broadsheet: Fraunces serif for headings and body, with Manrope for the numbers. Fraunces is bundled as static weights (Fraunces 9pt Regular/SemiBold/Bold/Black) instead of a variable font, because variable fonts silently fall back to the system face under the menu's renderer — which is why its serif didn't show in 2.10.0.
  • Gazette is set like a printed edition now, not a tinted theme. The panel is one flat cream page inside a 1pt ink border — no floating cards, no vibrancy wash — and every section is composed the way a newspaper column is. The provider card opens with a masthead: a folio line (edition number from the build, the date, how fresh the numbers are), the provider's name as a Fraunces Black nameplate, a deck of the headline percentages, and a double rule. The primary window is the lead story — a category tag and reset byline, the percentage as a big serif numeral, a flat printed gauge, the pace as the deck. The remaining windows and the balance run as two columns divided by a hairline: Weekly as a brief, the balance as a Money column with a dotted leader from "Balance" to the amount. Insights become In brief — coloured bullet squares with a bold lead word — with the forecast pulled out as an italic quote beside them. Resets, Explore and Export open under ink tags; action rows are tracked caps that invert to an ink block on hover; the page closes with a byline ("By Sriinnu", linking to GitHub), the imprint ("Runic 2.10.1 · Vol. 2 · No. 156") and an outlined About button. The overview is the front page: "The Runic Gazette" over leader rows (provider … percent) and a tagged 7-day chart. The provider tabs are hard-cornered category chips — the selected one a solid brand block with the paper knocked out of its label. Manrope is the body face (tracked caps for every label), Fraunces 9pt the display face, now bundled with its italic. The look is gated to Gazette; Terminal, System and every other theme are untouched.
